title: Artaxerxes Longimanus
summary: Artaxerxes Longimanus is dated in Raleigh's chronological table (1617), column Persia, by a yeere of the World. No tier 1–4 chronology dates this person.
description: Added from the Raleigh import (The History of the World, 1617). Raleigh is display-only. He gives a yeere of the World, not a BC year, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year. Raleigh is display-only and is not converted to BC.

standby.note: Standby placement only. Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology (1830, 2nd ed.) prints this BC/AD year on the reign entry (6. Artaxerxes Longimanus 41 464). It is not a sort year. No Anno Mundi, regnal length, or Julian Period figure was converted to obtain it.

reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 790b
reign.note: Year cell "4249 3567". To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 40 at the end of the name is the reign length he prints. The end year is not printed on this row. Column: Persia..

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 124; Manetho, ap. Syncellus, Chronicon 73 to 78, and Eusebius, Chronicle 16 and 17
reign.note: The text says Artaxerxes and does not say Longimanus. Placed on the existing 41-year Artaxerxes. Not placed on Artaxerxes Mnemon. Whether the edition means this king is open.

reign.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxvii
